verdict.headline: Hotter core inflation lifts the odds of an October rate hike, and debt-funded AI stocks fall hardest
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,718.94 (-1.11%), worst day since July, 0.7% above 7,666.45; Nasdaq 26,692.87 (-1.88%); Dow 51,621.48 (-0.09%); PHLX chips -4.3%, sixth straight loss; CoreWeave about -16%, Oracle about -9%; 10Y ~5.20% after a 5.323% intraday high; October hike odds ~44%; BTC $81,653.
verdict.rationale_short: September core CPI rose 0.3% for a second month against 0.2% expected, and headline inflation reached 3.7%, roughly doubling the odds of an October 28 hike to about 44%. The ten-year jumped to 5.323%, just under its 5.331% high, then gave the move back to about 5.20%, while the two-year held its rise, so the selling came from short-term rate expectations and credit markets rather than long-term yields. CoreWeave's bonds traded near 15% and Oracle's 2032 bond at 7.24%; CoreWeave fell about 16%, Dell 11% and Oracle 9%, and the chip index lost 4.3% for its sixth straight decline. This morning's read was right that a 0.3% core reading would push the ten-year back toward its high, and wrong that ASML's outlook had contained the chip selling to memory makers. The Dow's 0.09% loss shows the selling stayed concentrated in AI. TSMC's guidance and PPI on Thursday are the next tests; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the selling spreading beyond AI and chips.
verdict.lede_short: Core inflation beat forecasts for a second month, roughly doubling the odds of an October rate hike to about 44%. Long-term yields gave back their jump, but the AI companies that borrow most to build data centers fell hard, CoreWeave about 16% and Oracle 9%, and chip stocks lost 4.3% for a sixth straight day. The S&P 500 fell 1.1% and sits 0.7% above 7,666; TSMC and producer prices on Thursday decide whether it holds.

supporting_data.label: Core CPI rose 0.3% in September for a second month, against 0.2% expected, and headline inflation reached 3.7% — gasoline drove the headline, but the beat the Fed sets policy on came from core.
Odds of an October 28 rate hike roughly doubled to about 44% from 22%, and the ten-year briefly hit 5.323% — 0.8 basis points short of its 5.331% high before it gave the move back.
CoreWeave's bonds traded at yields near 15% and Oracle's 2032 bond at 7.24%, with Oracle closing down nearly 9% — lenders are charging the most-indebted AI builders more as hike odds rise.
The PHLX semiconductor index fell 4.3%, extending a six-session slide to 11.6% — the biggest drop of the run came on the day ASML's outlook lifted European chip stocks.
The S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Nasdaq 1.88% while the Dow lost 0.09% — the worst day since July, but the selling stayed concentrated in AI and chips.

Brent settled about $106.10, up 0.4%, as Houthi-Saudi clashes and Hormuz attacks offset more Russian diesel — about $1.40 above the $104.7 truce line, with gasoline already half of September's CPI gain.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 3.2%, about 7.5% below this month's record — a smaller loss than its debt-funded customers took on the hot CPI print.
Fell about 5.7%, the largest loss among the large chip designers as the chip index fell 4.3%.
Fell about 4.1% as the chip index extended its slide to six sessions and 11.6%.
Fell about 3.1% with the chip index.
Reports Thursday before the US open; guided third-quarter gross margin to 65-67% against 67.7% in the second quarter. Fourth-quarter guidance and 2027 spending decide whether chips steady.
At $81,653 on Crypto.com, down 1.8% over 24 hours from an $84,071 high, 1.7% above last Thursday's $80,320 low.

trade_setups.thesis: The chip index has fallen six sessions and 11.6%, the last 4.3% on hike odds and AI-borrower credit worries rather than any change in chip orders. TSMC's guidance is the first industry data since.
trade_setups.entry: PHLX chip index ~11,700; TSMC third-quarter gross margin guidance 65-67%; Nvidia about 7.5% below its record.
trade_setups.invalidation: Guidance held or raised would give chips a reason to steady that does not depend on rates; a cut would back the AI-funding worry with supplier numbers.

trade_setups.thesis: The index fell 1.11% to 7,718.94, 52 points above the level that separates an AI and chip sell-off from a broad one; the Dow's 0.09% loss shows the selling has stayed concentrated so far.
trade_setups.entry: S&P 500 7,718.94; 7,666.45 below; PPI expected +0.5% m/m and retail sales +0.3% Thursday.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 7,666.45 would show the selling spreading; a soft PPI and steady TSMC guidance would leave the index's loss confined to one sector.

trade_setups.thesis: CoreWeave's bonds yield near 15% and Oracle's 2032 bond 7.24%, while the ten-year ended near 5.20% after a 5.323% intraday high. The stress is in company credit, not long-term Treasury yields.
trade_setups.entry: CoreWeave bond yields near 15%; Oracle 2032 bond 7.24%; ten-year ~5.20%.
trade_setups.invalidation: Bond yields rising further with the ten-year steady would confirm a company-specific credit problem; easing yields would mean the equity losses rested mainly on hike odds.
